scenes.heading: Avoiding common first-year mistakes as a new agent or investor

sents.d: Avoiding common first-year mistakes as a new agent or investor
Most early mistakes come from inexperience with process, not lack of effort.
A common new-agent mistake is neglecting consistent lead generation once a few early deals come from an initial network, leading to a lead gap once that initial network is exhausted.

A common new-investor mistake is underestimating renovation costs and timelines, especially on a first flip or rehab project, which can quickly turn a promising deal into a loss if budgeted too optimistically.

Both agents and investors benefit from finding an experienced mentor early — someone who has navigated the specific mistakes you're likely to make — since learning from someone else's past mistakes is far less costly than repeating them yourself.

take: Keep prospecting, budget conservatively and learn from a mentor.
